correctness.rationale: With q=2^k atomic colors and pointed support data (c,S,T), a depth-one minterm homogeneity test recovers exactly T if |T|>1, and otherwise all such tests are true. In the latter case all opposite-side worlds have the identical successor set and color, so in fact all modal tests are true at every depth. For |T|>1 fix a in T: on the opposite side Δχ_b is a constant h_b, and Δ(χ_a ∧ Δχ_b) at the point holds precisely when h_b is false. These tests recover [S], including the singleton class. When |T|>1 the set of successor depth-two descriptors is then uniquely determined, including when |S|=1, so a formula induction proves stability. For each c there is one monochromatic-opposite descriptor and (2^q−q−1)·2^(q−1) others. Finite Boolean separation gives the powerset algebra at each depth. Varying valuations on K_{q,q} realizes all descriptors by repetition of colors; (c,C,C) forces at least q vertices on each side. Replacing S={c} by S={c,d} with the same non-singleton T proves sharpness. This covers k≥2 and validates the included k=1 example, with no assertion for k=0.
residual_risks: The companion script was inspected, not executed. Its symbolic refinement includes alphabets not arising from k Boolean letters and the concrete test includes sides of size one; these are diagnostic supersets, not the proof or a change of scope.
